name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 partisan lean with a sitting incumbent leaves almost no competitive path for the challenger
Crawford holds roughly $875,000 on hand to Green's about $6,000
Prediction markets price Crawford near 98 percent to win
No public polls or expert ratings; the race draws little outside attention
model.rationale: Crawford's incumbency, the district's heavy Republican lean, and a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage give Terri Green no visible path, and prediction markets agree this is a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Only a major outside-spending intervention or an unexpected scandal involving Crawford would put the race in play, and even then the district's steep partisan math would be hard to overcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's 1st District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Rick Crawford has held it since 2011. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised about $1.1 million and holding roughly $875,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Terri Green has raised about $112,000 and reported only about $6,000 in cash. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polling covers the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. The district's R+23 partisan lean, Crawford's untroubled renomination, and the challenger's minimal war chest all point the same direction. Everything indicates an easy Republican hold, with Crawford favored by roughly twenty points.
